answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer: No, please do not double to 80 miles or add doubles. Jumping from 40 to 80 in one week is a near-certain injury or deep fatigue, and the race is only 5 weeks away. Your club mate's 70 is the output of years of training; your body has handled around 40 to 53 for a few weeks and is still adapting. The way you catch up now is to protect what is working: hit the long run and the one quality day, keep the easy days easy, and sleep. That is what delivers sub 3:45, not a one-off big week.

new.analysis:
## What last week told me
You followed the plan line for line and the long run finished with only a 5.6 bpm drift over 15 miles, which says the engine is holding up. The Wednesday workout landed its marathon-pace miles at 8:30 to 8:40, which is exactly where sub 3:45 lives, so the fitness is tracking the goal.

## Why this shape next week
With the race 5 weeks out, this is the right window for the peak long run with marathon pace in it, which is the single most race-specific session we do. I kept Wednesday as a threshold day instead of more marathon pace so the two hard sessions stress different systems and Sunday gets your best legs. Volume rises a touch to about 45 miles, which is a normal step given you have already run 20 and 53 in recent weeks.

## How to run Sunday
Start the first 14 miles genuinely easy, around 9:55 per mile and heart rate under 150, then roll into 6 miles at 8:35. If the marathon-pace block feels like a 7 out of 10 effort, that is right; if it climbs to a 9, back off and finish the distance easy rather than forcing the pace. That restraint early is what makes the finish possible.
